All:
# Local officials, who work in city or county government and are involved
# in local decisions about land use, zoning, and development related to
# energy projects. How honest and transparent is this group in what it says
# and does regarding energy projects?
#
# S3OK Public Survey, University of Oklahoma Institute for Public
# Policy Research and Analysis. Rebuilds this chart from the public
# wave files and nothing else.
# Wave 8.

library(tidyverse)
library(srvyr)

# Read as character: a column that is empty for its first thousand rows
# is otherwise guessed logical, which turns every real value after it
# into NA.
wave_8 <- read_csv(
  "Public_Wave_8_Survey_Data.csv",
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character())
)

d <- bind_rows(
  wave_8 |>
    transmute(
      p_id,
      resp = loc_hon
    )
) |>
  filter(!is.na(resp))

# The survey is a panel, so one person can answer in several waves. The
# design clusters on the panelist: percentages are unweighted shares of
# responses, and the intervals allow for repeated answers.
est <- d |>
  as_survey_design(ids = p_id) |>
  group_by(resp) |>
  summarise(
    p = survey_prop(proportion = TRUE, vartype = "ci"),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

est <- est |>
  mutate(
    p = 100 * p, p_low = 100 * p_low, p_upp = 100 * p_upp,
    resp = factor(
      resp,
      levels = c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5"),
      labels = c("Not at all", "Slightly", "Moderately", "Very", "Extremely")
    )
  )

ggplot(est, aes(x = p, y = fct_rev(resp))) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(xmin = p_low, xmax = p_upp),
    width = 0.2, linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  labs(
    title = str_wrap(paste(
      "Local officials, who work in city or county government and",
      "are involved in local decisions about land use, zoning, and",
      "development related to energy projects. How honest and",
      "transparent is this group in what it says and does",
      "regarding energy projects?"
    ), 70),
    x = "Share of respondents (%)",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

library(srvyr)

# Read as character: a column that is empty for its first thousand rows
# is otherwise guessed logical, which turns every real value after it
# into NA.
wave_8 <- read_csv(
  "Public_Wave_8_Survey_Data.csv",
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character())
)

d <- bind_rows(
  wave_8 |>
    transmute(
      p_id,
      IDEOLOGY = case_when(
        ideol %in% c("1", "2", "3") ~ "Liberal",
        ideol == "4"                ~ "Moderate",
        ideol %in% c("5", "6", "7") ~ "Conservative"
      ),
      resp = loc_hon
    )
) |>
  filter(!is.na(resp), !is.na(IDEOLOGY)) |>
  # A group with fewer than 20 respondents on this question is not charted.
  filter(n() >= 20, .by = IDEOLOGY)

# The survey is a panel, so one person can answer in several waves. The
# design clusters on the panelist: percentages are unweighted shares of
# responses, and the intervals allow for repeated answers.
est <- d |>
  as_survey_design(ids = p_id) |>
  group_by(IDEOLOGY, resp) |>
  summarise(
    p = survey_prop(proportion = TRUE, vartype = "ci"),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

est <- est |>
  mutate(
    p = 100 * p, p_low = 100 * p_low, p_upp = 100 * p_upp,
    resp = factor(
      resp,
      levels = c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5"),
      labels = c("Not at all", "Slightly", "Moderately", "Very", "Extremely")
    ),
    IDEOLOGY = factor(
      IDEOLOGY,
      levels = c("Liberal", "Moderate", "Conservative")
    )
  )

ggplot(est, aes(x = p, y = fct_rev(resp), fill = IDEOLOGY)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge2(reverse = TRUE), width = 0.8) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(xmin = p_low, xmax = p_upp),
    position = position_dodge2(reverse = TRUE),
    width = 0.2, linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  labs(
    title = str_wrap(paste(
      "Local officials, who work in city or county government and",
      "are involved in local decisions about land use, zoning, and",
      "development related to energy projects. How honest and",
      "transparent is this group in what it says and does",
      "regarding energy projects?"
    ), 70),
    x = "Share of respondents (%)",
    y = NULL,
    fill = "Ideology"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
